title: Fructose- and sucrose- but not glucose-sweetened beverages promote hepatic de novo lipogenesis: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Geidl-Flueck B, Hochuli M, Németh Á, Eberl A, Derron N, Köfeler HC, et al.
population: Healthy men aged 18 to 30 years with BMI below 24 kg/m2 in Zurich; 94 of 126 randomised completed
funder: This study was funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (No. 144204), Vontobel Foundation, Rhyner Bangerter Foundation, Promedica Foundation, Uniscientia Foundation, Prof. Otto Beisheim-Foundation, Jubiläumsstiftung Swiss Life, Philhuman Foundation and the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education (No. BMWFW-10.420/0005-WF/V/3c/2017).
inKindSupport: Molkerei Biedermann AG provided the beverages in coded containers; the Swiss technology testing service, Dietikon, performed quality control; payment terms are not stated.
authorConflicts: The authors declared that no conflicts of interest exist with regard to this study; ICMJE forms not read.
result: Described as double-blind; the control group abstained from sugar-sweetened beverages and received no placebo. 80 g per day of fructose, sucrose or glucose in three 200 ml beverages for 7 weeks. Median basal hepatic fractional secretion rate of newly synthesised VLDL palmitate (%/day): fructose 19.7 (P=0.013), sucrose 20.8 (P=0.0015), glucose 11.0 (P=0.16), control 9.1. Total energy intake did not change; fasting triglyceride, glucose and insulin did not change; liver fat was not measured.
